page: Microsoft Azure D2d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU is equipped with a 35 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 77 GB of local storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the D2d_v4 is positioned in the lower tiers for multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, fall into the bottom 10% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 12.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 8.99 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are similarly limited, with Redis achieving 1.75 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2d_v4 offers a balanced resource density for entry-level general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of high-performance compute or memory-optimized instances. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core scaling and lower memory bandwidth, which makes it less suitable for parallel processing or large-scale data manipulation. The inclusion of 77 GB of local storage provides a dedicated scratch space, but the overall resource profile is designed for low-intensity applications.

This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Appropriate applications include basic web serving, development and testing environments, small-scale single-threaded applications, and low-traffic database hosting. It is not recommended for high-throughput database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or intensive multi-threaded compilation tasks.
